stem: A safety-control system assigns high integrity to validated control commands and low integrity to untrusted telemetry imported from an external partner. The design goal is to prevent the high-integrity control process from consuming low-integrity data unless it passes an approved validation path. Which classic model rule MOST directly expresses this integrity requirement?
decision_point: apply the Biba integrity rule that prevents higher-integrity subjects from reading lower-integrity information directly
misconceptions: Bell-LaPadula is the primary integrity model
integrity levels matter only when writing

originality.authoring_note: Sibling of the released Bell-LaPadula confidentiality item, but this scenario tests Biba's integrity-oriented no-read-down principle.

options: Bell-LaPadula's no-read-up rule, because all multilevel access rules are confidentiality rules
Biba's no-write-up rule, because the concern is a high-integrity process reading external telemetry
Biba's simple integrity/no-read-down principle, because a higher-integrity subject should not directly consume lower-integrity information without an approved trusted path
No formal integrity rule applies if the external telemetry is encrypted in transit
explanation: Biba is integrity-oriented. Its simple integrity property is commonly summarized as no read down: a higher-integrity subject should not directly read lower-integrity information that could contaminate trusted processing.
distractor_rationales: Bell-LaPadula is classically confidentiality-oriented and its no-read-up rule addresses a different information-flow objective.
Biba's no-write-up rule constrains writes toward higher-integrity objects; the stated decision is whether a high-integrity subject may read lower-integrity input.

Biba is integrity-oriented. Its simple integrity property is commonly summarized as no read down: a higher-integrity subject should not directly read lower-integrity information that could contaminate trusted processing.
Encryption protects transport confidentiality/integrity properties but does not determine the trust or integrity classification of the source information.

stem: A serverless order-processing application uses twenty cloud functions. Every function runs under the same highly privileged execution role because the team says short-lived functions are too temporary to justify separate permissions. One low-risk image-resize function is compromised and can now read payment secrets and modify the order database. What is the BEST architectural correction?
decision_point: treat each serverless workload as a distinct security principal with least privilege and scoped secret/data access
misconceptions: short execution duration removes privilege risk
shared roles simplify security without increasing blast radius
network isolation alone fixes overprivileged identities

originality.authoring_note: Original serverless architecture scenario focused on workload identity and privilege blast radius rather than container or VM isolation.

options: Keep the shared role because short-lived functions cannot retain attacker access long enough to create material risk

Give each function or tightly related workload an appropriately scoped identity and permissions, restrict secret and data access to required resources, and monitor the resulting service-to-service actions
Move all functions into one larger function so only one identity exists
Rely only on a web application firewall because network filtering replaces authorization between cloud services
explanation: Serverless workloads still execute with identities and permissions. Overbroad shared roles create lateral access and blast radius, so least-privilege workload identities and scoped secret/data permissions are key architectural controls.
distractor_rationales: Short execution time does not prevent a compromised function from immediately abusing whatever privileges its execution identity possesses.

Serverless workloads still execute with identities and permissions. Overbroad shared roles create lateral access and blast radius, so least-privilege workload identities and scoped secret/data permissions are key architectural controls.
Combining functions can increase coupling and privilege scope rather than correcting authorization boundaries.
A WAF can filter some inbound traffic but does not replace cloud IAM controls governing service identities and resource permissions.

stem: A smart-card implementation uses a secure cryptographic chip. During lab testing, researchers discover that carefully timed voltage glitches can cause the chip to skip a verification step and occasionally emit a faulty signature that reveals information useful for recovering the private key. What is the BEST mitigation direction?
decision_point: mitigate physical fault injection with resilient implementation and hardware controls rather than changing key length alone

originality.authoring_note: Original physical fault-injection scenario distinct from released timing and chosen-ciphertext implementation attacks.

options: Increase only the private-key length because fault injection is primarily a brute-force attack
Add TLS between the card reader and application because encrypted transport prevents voltage faults inside the chip

Use fault-resistant hardware and implementation techniques such as voltage/clock anomaly detection, redundant or verified cryptographic computation, secure failure behavior, and retesting under physical fault conditions
Keep the implementation unchanged because the underlying signature algorithm is mathematically sound
explanation: Fault injection attacks target implementation behavior by inducing abnormal computation. Countermeasures focus on detecting or resisting faults, verifying results, failing safely, and validating the physical implementation under adversarial conditions.
distractor_rationales: Key length changes brute-force cost but does not prevent induced computation faults.
Transport encryption does not stop an attacker who physically manipulates voltage or clock behavior at the cryptographic device.

Fault injection attacks target implementation behavior by inducing abnormal computation. Countermeasures focus on detecting or resisting faults, verifying results, failing safely, and validating the physical implementation under adversarial conditions.
A sound algorithm can still be undermined by a vulnerable physical implementation.

stem: Production engineers keep permanent administrator membership because any one of them may be paged overnight. The organization has strong MFA and logging, but most engineers use the elevated role only a few times per month. A compromise of any engineer therefore exposes standing production privilege continuously. Which redesign BEST reduces this risk without preventing emergency work?
decision_point: replace unnecessary standing privilege with short-lived, strongly authenticated, policy-controlled elevation and a separately governed emergency path
misconceptions: shared emergency credentials are preferable to attributable elevation

originality.authoring_note: Original just-in-time privileged-access scenario focused on standing-role reduction and emergency availability.

options: Keep permanent administrator membership because MFA eliminates the risk created by standing privilege
Move all engineers to a shared administrator credential stored in a team password manager
Remove all privileged access permanently and require executives to make every production change

Use just-in-time elevation with strong authentication, defined eligibility and approval/context rules, short expiration, full attribution and logging, plus a separately controlled break-glass path for genuine emergencies
explanation: Just-in-time access reduces the window in which a compromised normal account carries privileged authority while preserving operational availability through controlled, attributable elevation and emergency procedures.
distractor_rationales: MFA improves authentication assurance but does not remove the blast radius of continuously assigned privilege after a session or account is compromised.
Shared administrator credentials weaken individual accountability and do not reduce the standing privilege problem.
Eliminating all operational privilege makes legitimate response impractical and does not represent a balanced access design.

Just-in-time access reduces the window in which a compromised normal account carries privileged authority while preserving operational availability through controlled, attributable elevation and emergency procedures.
